title: Chow's lemma over a qcqs base
statement: Let $S$ be a quasi-compact scheme [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] which is quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], and let $f:X\to S$ be a separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] morphism of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Then there are a finite set $N$, a scheme $\widetilde X$, a proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] morphism $\pi:\widetilde X\to X$ and an immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] $i_S:\widetilde X\to\mathbf P^N_S$ such that $q_S\circ i_S=f\circ\pi$, where $\mathbf P^N_S$ is projective space with homogeneous coordinates indexed by $N$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] and $q_S:\mathbf P^N_S\to S$ is its projection.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-chow-finite-type] to $f$. Its hypotheses are exactly ours: $S$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $f$ separated and of finite type. It gives an integer $n\ge0$, a scheme $X'$, a proper surjective morphism $\pi:X'\to X$ and an immersion $j:X'\to\mathbf P^n_S=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ with $p\circ j=f\circ\pi$, where $p$ is the projection. By [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], the classical $\mathbf P^n_S$ is $\mathbf P(\{0,\dots,n\};S)$, with the first projection as structure morphism. Put $N=\{0,\dots,n\}$, a finite set, $\widetilde X=X'$, $i_S=j$ and $q_S=p$. Then $\pi$ is proper and surjective, $i_S$ is an immersion into the projective space with homogeneous coordinates indexed by $N$, and $q_S\circ i_S=f\circ\pi$. These are all the requested data. The cited node proves Stacks 0202 along this unit's paragraph-3 route: envelope 01ZJ, Noetherian approximation 01ZA, separated finitely presented descent 01ZM/01ZQ, Noetherian Chow 0200, base change back to $S$ and pullback to $X$.
